Surface materials

Source: R/lights-3d.R
material_3d.Rd

A material sets how strongly a face reflects the ambient, diffuse and specular light of lights_3d(). The presets follow MATLAB's material: "matte" (MATLAB dull), "shiny" and "metal", with the ambient and diffuse strengths taken relative to dull so that "matte" reproduces plain Lambert shading. The specular highlight is Blinn's (1977) halfway term specular * max(0, n . h)^shininess; its colour moves from white to the face colour as specular_colour goes from 1 to 0 (MATLAB's SpecularColorReflectance). back colours the back side of faces, the side a face's normal points away from; NULL lights both sides alike.

Usage

material_3d(
  type = "matte",
  ambient = NULL,
  diffuse = NULL,
  specular = NULL,
  shininess = NULL,
  specular_colour = NULL,
  back = NULL,
  style = "standard",
  bands = 3L,
  breaks = NULL,
  specular_steps = NULL,
  cool = "#0000AA",
  warm = "#AAAA00",
  alpha = 0.2,
  beta = 0.6,
  normal_space = "model"
)

Arguments

type

Preset: "matte", "shiny" or "metal".

ambient, diffuse, specular

Nonnegative strengths; NULL keeps the preset.

shininess

Positive specular exponent; NULL keeps the preset.

specular_colour

Specular colour reflectance in [0, 1]; NULL keeps the preset.

back

NULL or one colour for the back side of faces.

style

"standard", "toon", "gooch" or "normals".

bands

Number of toon bands, at least two.

breaks

NULL or increasing toon band breaks in degrees in (0, 180).

specular_steps

Whether the highlight is a flat spot; NULL takes TRUE for toon and FALSE otherwise.

cool, warm

Gooch colours.

alpha, beta

Gooch weights of the fill in the cool and warm colours.

normal_space

Frame of the normal colours: "model", "camera" or "light".

Value

A material for the material argument of the surface layers.

Details

style selects an illustrative response, computed by the same shading kernel in the vector and raster backends and the viewer:

  • "toon" quantises each light's diffuse response into bands equal steps of the cosine, or at the angles breaks (degrees from the light, increasing, at most seven; a normal exactly at a break, within 1e-6 in cosine, falls in the darker band), as ggcube's ramp_steps(). With the signed modes of lights_3d() the steps divide the signed level instead. specular_steps = TRUE (the default for toon) turns the highlight into a flat spot where Blinn's term reaches one half.

  • "gooch" is the cool-to-warm shading of Gooch et al. (1998): the colour blends from cool + alpha * fill to warm + beta * fill as (1 + n . l) / 2 goes from 0 to 1, averaged over the lights; the defaults are the paper's k_blue = (0, 0, 0.4) and k_yellow = (0.4, 0.4, 0) in linear light with alpha = 0.2, beta = 0.6.

  • "normals" replaces the fill by the unit normal encoded as (n + 1) / 2 in sRGB (three.js MeshNormalMaterial), in the panel's axes (normal_space = "model"), the camera's right, up and toward axes ("camera"), or a frame whose third axis points at the first contributing light ("light"). It takes no light and no specular term, and the layer's fill legend is dropped.

Styles need a light: with coord_3d(light = NULL) faces keep their fill. In the path tracer, illustrative surfaces return the shared kernel's colour at the hit point and terminate the path, including indirect hits.

References

Gooch, Gooch, Shirley, Cohen (1998). A non-photorealistic lighting model for automatic technical illustration. SIGGRAPH '98, 447-452. doi:10.1145/280814.280950

Examples

material_3d("shiny")
material_3d("metal", back = "grey40")
material_3d(style = "toon", breaks = c(40, 75))
d <- expand.grid(x = seq(-1, 1, length.out = 12), y = seq(-1, 1, length.out = 12))
d$z <- with(d, x^2 - y^2)
p <- ggplot2::ggplot(d, ggplot2::aes(x, y, z = z))
p + geom_surface_3d(shading = "smooth", material = material_3d("shiny")) + coord_3d()
p + geom_surface_3d(fill = "grey60", colour = NA, material = material_3d(style = "gooch")) + coord_3d()
p + geom_surface_3d(fill = "tomato", colour = NA, material = material_3d(style = "toon", bands = 4)) + coord_3d()
p + geom_surface_3d(colour = NA, shading = "smooth", material = material_3d(style = "normals")) + coord_3d()
